'''Bitwarden''' is a [[freemium]] [[open-source software|open-source]] [[Password manager|password management service]] that is used to store sensitive information, such as website credentials, in an [[Encryption|encrypted]] vault. It is owned and developed by Bitwarden, Inc.<ref>{{Cite web |title=About Us {{!}} Bitwarden |url=https://bitwarden.com/about/ |access-date=28 October 2025 |archive-date=12 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251112021653/https://bitwarden.com/about/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Siddiqui |first=Aamir |date=2024-05-02 |title=Bitwarden launches its own free and open-source Authenticator app |url=https://www.androidauthority.com/bitwarden-authenticator-app-free-open-source-3439120/ |access-date=2026-05-30 |website=Android Authority |language=en}}</ref>

== Functionalities ==
Bitwarden uses client-side [[zero-knowledge encryption]], meaning the company cannot see its users' data.<ref name="theregister/4306575">{{cite news |last1=Jones |first1=Connor |title=Password managers don’t protect secrets if pwned |url=https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/02/16/password-managers-dont-protect-secrets-if-pwned/4306575 |access-date=4 September 2026 |work=[[The Register]] |date=16 February 2026}}</ref> This is achieved by [[End-to-end encryption|end-to-end encrypting]] data with [[AES-CBC]] 256-bit and by using [[PBKDF2]] [[SHA-2|SHA-256]]/[[Argon2]]id to derive the encryption key.<ref>{{cite web |title=Encryption {{!}} Bitwarden Help & Support |work=Bitwarden.com |url= https://bitwarden.com/help/what-encryption-is-used/ |url-status=live |access-date=22 February 2023 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230222185152/https://bitwarden.com/help/what-encryption-is-used/ |archive-date=22 February 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=How End-to-End Encryption Paves the Way for Zero Knowledge |url=https://bitwarden.com/blog/end-to-end-encryption-and-zero-knowledge/ |access-date=7 June 2024 |work=Bitwarden.com |archive-date=7 June 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240607135145/https://bitwarden.com/blog/end-to-end-encryption-and-zero-knowledge/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

To [[Login|log in]], a user can use an email-address and password combination, [[biometric]] authentication, [[two-factor authentication]] (2FA), [[Passkey (authentication)|passkey]], [[single sign-on]], or [[passwordless login]] via notification approval on a mobile/desktop device.<ref name="CNet 1 May 2022" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=30 September 2020 |title=Bitwarden launches SSO authentication to integrate password security with identity providers |url= https://bitwarden.com/blog/post/bitwarden-launches-sso-authentication/ |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220427191331/https://bitwarden.com/blog/bitwarden-launches-sso-authentication/ |archive-date=27 April 2022 |work=Bitwarden Blog}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=23 February 2023 |title=Access Your Bitwarden Vault Without a Password |url= https://bitwarden.com/blog/access-your-bitwarden-vault-without-a-password/ |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230731113501/https://bitwarden.com/blog/access-your-bitwarden-vault-without-a-password/ |archive-date=31 July 2023 |work=The Bitwarden Blog}}</ref>

Additional client functionality includes: import of data from more than 50 password managers (such as [[LastPass]], [[1Password]], and [[Keeper (password manager)|Keeper]]) passkey management; export to [[JSON]], encrypted JSON, and [[Comma-separated values|CSV]] formats;<ref name="PCMag 15 March 2022">{{cite web |title=Bitwarden Review |date=15 March 2022 |work=[[PCMag]] |url= https://www.pcmag.com/reviews/bitwarden |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220818122238/https://www.pcmag.com/reviews/bitwarden |archive-date=18 August 2022}}</ref> a [[random password generator]]; [[autofill]] of login and other forms; integration with [[email alias]] services; ability to sync across unlimited platforms and devices; storage of an unlimited number of items; and storing a variety of information beyond [[User (computing)|username]]-and-[[password]] pairs, including passkeys, [[Time-based one-time password|TOTP]] seeds, [[Debit card|debit]] and [[credit card]] numbers, billing data and other identity information, and secure notes (free-form text). Each item type can be extended by custom fields and file attachments, though these are restricted by file size depending on the subscription plan.<ref name="CNet 1 May 2022">{{cite web |title=Bitwarden Review: The Best Free Password Manager for 2022 |date=1 May 2022 |work=[[CNet]] |url= https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/bitwarden-review-the-best-free-password-manager-for-2022/ |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220907050911/https://www.cnet.com/tech/services-and-software/bitwarden-review-the-best-free-password-manager-for-2022/ |archive-date=7 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Store Secure Notes, Credit Cards, & Identities In Your Bitwarden Vault {{!}} Bitwarden |url=https://bitwarden.com/blog/notes-cards-identities-released |access-date=26 September 2021 |work=Bitwarden Blog |archive-date=26 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210926065938/https://bitwarden.com/blog/notes-cards-identities-released/ |url-status=live }}</ref> A feature called "Send" allows sharing of end-to-end encrypted [[text message]]s (free version) and files (paid versions). Any sent item optionally can be set with an expiration date, a maximum access limit, and a password.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Password Strength Testing Tool |url=https://bitwarden.com/password-generator/ |work=Bitwarden |access-date=29 June 2020 |archive-date=12 December 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201212203449/https://bitwarden.com/password-generator/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Username & Password Generator {{!}} Bitwarden Help & Support |url=https://bitwarden.com/help/generator/#generate-a-username |work=Bitwarden |access-date=4 August 2022 |archive-date=27 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227225836/https://bitwarden.com/help/generator/#generate-a-username |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=18 October 2022 |title=Add Privacy and Security Using Email Aliases With Bitwarden |url= https://bitwarden.com/blog/add-privacy-and-security-using-email-aliases-with-bitwarden/ |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20221126204057/https://bitwarden.com/blog/add-privacy-and-security-using-email-aliases-with-bitwarden/ |archive-date=26 November 2022 |work=The Bitwarden Blog}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=About Send |work=Bitwarden.com |url= https://bitwarden.com/help/about-send/ |url-status=live |access-date=10 September 2022 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220427054548/https://bitwarden.com/help/about-send/ |archive-date=27 April 2022}}</ref> The Password Checkup tool uses zxcvbn to assess [[password strength]].<ref name="Hutchinson2024">{{Cite book |last1=Hutchinson |first1=Adryana |last2=Munyendo |first2=Collins W. |last3=Aviv |first3=Adam J |last4=Mayer |first4=Peter |chapter=An Analysis of Password Managers' Password Checkup Tools |date=2024-05-11 |title=Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems |series=CHI EA '24 |location=New York, NY, USA |publisher=Association for Computing Machinery |pages=1–7 |doi=10.1145/3613905.3650741 |isbn=979-8-4007-0331-7|doi-access=free }}</ref> It detects credential breaches by querying the [[Have I Been Pwned?]] database.<ref name="Hutchinson2024"/>

Bitwarden implements credential sharing through collections within an organization. As of 2024 collections in a given organization are encrypted using the same organizational secret key, meaning that privilege separation is enforced at the authorization layer rather than through distinct encryption keys for each collection.<ref>{{cite arXiv |last1=Fábrega |first1=Andrés |last2=Namavari |first2=Armin |last3=Agarwal |first3=Rachit |last4=Nassi |first4=Ben |last5=Ristenpart |first5=Thomas |title=Exploiting Leakage in Password Managers via Injection Attacks |date=2024 |class=cs.CR |eprint=2408.07054v1 }}</ref>

== Availability ==
The platform hosts multiple client applications, including a [[Browser user interface|web interface]], [[desktop application]]s, [[browser extension]]s, [[mobile app]]s, and a [[command-line interface]].<ref name="Downloads">{{cite web |last=Wallen |first=Jack |date=31 May 2018 |title=How to install and use the Bitwarden command line password manager |url=https://www.techrepublic.com/article/how-to-install-and-use-the-bitwarden-command-line-password-manager/ |access-date= |work=TechRepublic |archive-date=5 August 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240805040250/https://www.techrepublic.com/article/how-to-install-and-use-the-bitwarden-command-line-password-manager/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Bitwarden can be operated on web interfaces, desktop applications ([[Windows]], [[MacOS]], and [[Linux]]), browser extensions ([[Google Chrome|Chrome]], [[Firefox]], [[Safari (web browser)|Safari]], [[Microsoft Edge|Edge]], [[Opera (web browser)|Opera]], [[Vivaldi (web browser)|Vivaldi]], [[Arc (web browser)|Arc]], [[Brave (web browser)|Brave]] and [[Tor (network)#Tor Browser|Tor]]), or mobile apps ([[Android (operating system)|Android]], [[iOS]], [[iPadOS]] and [[watchOS]]).<ref name="CNet 1 May 2022" /> 50 languages and dialects are supported, although not all of them are available on all clients.<ref>{{cite web |title=Localization |work=Bitwarden.com |url= https://bitwarden.com/help/localization/ |url-status=live |access-date=10 September 2022 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220910134930/https://bitwarden.com/help/localization/ |archive-date=10 September 2022}}</ref>

The platform also offers a free US or European [[Cloud computing|cloud-hosted]] synchronisation service, as well as the ability to [[Self-hosting (web services)|self-host]].<ref>{{cite web |date=2 November 2022 |title=Bitwarden password manager review |url= https://www.techradar.com/reviews/bitwarden |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220908174109/https://www.techradar.com/reviews/bitwarden |archive-date=8 September 2022 |work=[[TechRadar]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Brinkmann |first1=Martin |date=27 July 2023 |title=How to migrate your Bitwarden vaults from US to EU storage |work=[[Ghacks]] Technology News |url= https://www.ghacks.net/2023/07/27/how-to-migrate-your-bitwarden-vaults-from-us-to-eu-storage/ |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230727195326/https://www.ghacks.net/2023/07/27/how-to-migrate-your-bitwarden-vaults-from-us-to-eu-storage/ |archive-date=27 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Server Geographies |url= https://bitwarden.com/help/server-geographies/ |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230726121107/https://bitwarden.com/help/server-geographies/ |archive-date=26 July 2023 |access-date=28 July 2023 |work=Bitwarden.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=19 April 2022 |title=Self-hosting Bitwarden on DigitalOcean |url= https://bitwarden.com/blog/digitalocean-marketplace/ |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220617050116/https://bitwarden.com/blog/digitalocean-marketplace/ |archive-date=17 June 2022 |work=The Bitwarden Blog}}</ref>

=== Security audits ===
Third-party security audits are conducted annually and a [[Bug bounty program|vulnerability disclosure program]] is also established.<ref name="hackerone" /><ref name="BW-Compliance-2022-09-09" />

In June 2018, [[Cliqz GmbH|Cliqz]] performed a privacy and security review of the Bitwarden for Firefox browser extension and concluded that it would not negatively impact their users.<ref name="Cliqz extension review" /> In October of that year, Bitwarden completed a security assessment, [[code audit]], and cryptographic analysis from third-party security auditing firm [[Cure53]].<ref name="bitwarden-audit">{{cite web |date=12 November 2018 |title=Bitwarden Completes Third-party Security Audit |url= https://blog.bitwarden.com/bitwarden-completes-third-party-security-audit-c1cc81b6d33 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20181112153110/https://blog.bitwarden.com/bitwarden-completes-third-party-security-audit-c1cc81b6d33 |archive-date=12 November 2018 |access-date=26 November 2018 |work=The Bitwarden Blog}}</ref><ref name="ghacks-bitwarden-audit">{{cite web |last1=Brinkmann |first1=Martin |date=13 November 2018 |title=Results of Bitwarden security audit published |work=[[Ghacks]] Technology News |url=https://www.ghacks.net/2018/11/13/results-of-bitwarden-security-audit-published/ |access-date=26 November 2018 |archive-date=14 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181114192945/https://www.ghacks.net/2018/11/13/results-of-bitwarden-security-audit-published/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="macobserver-bitwarden-audit">{{cite web |date=12 November 2018 |title=Bitwarden Passes Third Party Security Audit |url=https://www.macobserver.com/news/bitwarden-security-audit/ |access-date=26 November 2018 |work=The Mac Observer |archive-date=26 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181126221445/https://www.macobserver.com/news/bitwarden-security-audit/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Heiderich |first1=Mario |last2=Inführ |first2=Alex |last3=Kobeissi |first3=Nadim |last4=Hippert |first4=Norman |last5=Kinugawa |first5=Masato |date=8 November 2018 |title=Pentest-Report: Bitwarden Password Manager 11.2018 |work=[[Cure53]].com |url= https://cure53.de/pentest-report_bitwarden.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url= In July 2020, Bitwarden completed another security audit from security firm Insight Risk Consulting to evaluate the security of the Bitwarden network perimeter as well as penetration testing and vulnerability assessments against Bitwarden web services and applications. In August 2021, Bitwarden announced that network assessment (security assessment and penetration testing) for 2021<!-- Although the ref itself mentioned both 2020 & 2021 audits, the ref has been updated since its original post on July 22, 2020, making using this ref awkward since it announced the 2020 audit in 2020, and then updated to include both 2020 & 2021 in 2021.--> had been completed again by Insight Risk Consulting.<ref name="PCMag 15 March 2022" /><ref>{{cite web |date=2 August 2021 |title=Bitwarden 2020 and 2021 Security Audits are Complete|work=The Bitwarden Blog |url= https://bitwarden.com/blog/bitwarden-network-security-assessment-2020/ |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220818191236/https://bitwarden.com/blog/bitwarden-network-security-assessment-2020/ |archive-date=18 August 2022}}</ref>

In February 2023, Bitwarden released network security assessment and security assessment reports that were conducted by Cure53 again in May and October 2022 respectively.<ref>{{cite web |last=Spearrin == Reception ==
In January 2021, in its first password-protection program comparison, ''[[U.S. News & World Report]]'' selected Bitwarden as "Best Password Manager".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kinney |first=Jeff |title=Best Password Managers of 2021 |date=12 January 2021 |work=[[U.S. News & World Report]] |url= https://www.usnews.com/360-reviews/password-managers |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210115103910/https://www.usnews.com/360-reviews/password-managers |archive-date=15 January 2021}}</ref> A month later, with Bitwarden competitor [[LastPass]] about to remove a feature from its free version, ''[[CNet]]'' recommended Bitwarden as the best free app for password synchronization across multiple devices,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Broida |first=Rick |title=This is the best free password manager alternative to LastPass |work=[[CNet]] |url=https://www.cnet.com/news/this-is-the-best-free-password-manager-alternative-to-lastpass/ |access-date=17 February 2021 |archive-date=16 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210216235203/https://www.cnet.com/news/this-is-the-best-free-password-manager-alternative-to-lastpass/ |url-status=live }}</ref> while ''[[Lifehacker]]'' recommended it as "the best password manager for most people".<ref name="Lifehacker recommendation">{{cite web |last=Murphy |first=David |title=Bitwarden Is Now the Best Free Alternative to LastPass |date=18 February 2021 |work=[[Lifehacker]] |url=https://lifehacker.com/bitwarden-is-now-the-best-free-alternative-to-lastpass-1846289833 |access-date=19 February 2021 |archive-date=18 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210218232405/https://lifehacker.com/bitwarden-is-now-the-best-free-alternative-to-lastpass-1846289833 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Reviewers have praised the features offered in the software's free version, and (mostly) the low price of the premium tier compared to other managers.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="Long 2021">{{Cite web |last=Long |first=Emily |date=22 April 2021 |title=Bitwarden password manager review |work=[[Tom's Guide]] |url= https://www.tomsguide.com/reviews/bitwarden |url-status=live |access-date=6 May 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210424181342/https://www.tomsguide.com/reviews/bitwarden |archive-date=24 April 2021}}</ref><ref name="Lamont 2020">{{Cite web |last=Lamont |first=Jonathan |title=Bitwarden offers excellent password management tools with great value |date=2 August 2020 |work=MobileSyrup |url=https://mobilesyrup.com/2020/08/02/bitwarden-password-manager-review/ |access-date=6 May 2021 |archive-date=23 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210623190610/https://mobilesyrup.com/2020/08/02/bitwarden-password-manager-review/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Pathak 2021">{{Cite web |last=Pathak |first=Khamosh |title=Bitwarden Is the Best Free Alternative to LastPass |date=27 February 2021 |work=How-to Geek |url=https://www.howtogeek.com/715490/bitwarden-is-the-best-free-alternative-to-lastpass/ |access-date=6 May 2021 |archive-date=6 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210506193756/https://www.howtogeek.com/715490/bitwarden-is-the-best-free-alternative-to-lastpass/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The product was named the best "budget pick" in a ''[[Wirecutter (website)|Wirecutter]]'' password manager comparison.<ref>{{Cite news |title=The Best Password Managers |date=5 February 2021 |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/wirecutter/reviews/best-password-managers/ |access-date=6 May 2021 |archive-date=19 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220119205043/https://www.nytimes.com/wirecutter/reviews/best-password-managers/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Bitwarden's secure open-source implementation was also praised by reviewers.<ref name="Long 2021" /><ref name="Pathak 2021" />

Nevertheless, ''[[Tom's Guide]]'' found some features to be less intuitive than they could be,<ref name="Long 2021" /> while ''[[PC Magazine]]'' criticized the price of the business tier as too high.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rubenking |first=Neil J. |date=19 June 2019 |title=Bitwarden Review |work=PCMag |url= https://www.pcmag.com/reviews/bitwarden |url-status=live |access-date=6 May 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200207204408/https://www.pcmag.com/reviews/bitwarden |archive-date=7 February 2020}}</ref>

Bitwarden was highlighted by [[Süddeutsche Zeitung]] in its 2025 overview of leading self-hosted password managers as a solution that offers users increased security and full control by allowing the entire vault to be operated on their own server.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-09 |title=Bester Self-Hosted Passwort-Manager 2025 |url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/erfahrungen/passwort-manager/self-hosted/ |access-date=2025-11-22 |language=de |archive-date=19 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251119211227/https://www.sueddeutsche.de/erfahrungen/passwort-manager/self-hosted/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==History==

=== 2016–2017 ===
Bitwarden debuted in August 2016 with an initial release of mobile applications for [[iOS]] and [[Android (operating system)|Android]], browser extensions for [[Google Chrome|Chrome]] and [[Opera (web browser)|Opera]], and a Web-based "vault" (encrypted database). The browser extension for [[Firefox]] was later launched in February 2017.<ref name="firefox-release">{{cite web |title=Bitwarden: Add-ons for Firefox |url=https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/bitwarden-password-manager/versions/1.9.8 |work=Addons.[[Mozilla]].org |access-date=26 November 2018 |archive-date=21 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170821195830/https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/bitwarden-password-manager/versions/1.9.8 |url-status=live }}</ref> The same month, the [[Brave (web browser)|Brave web browser]] began including the Bitwarden extension as an optional replacement password manager.<ref name="brave-features">{{cite web |title=Brave Features |url=https://brave.com/features/ |work=[[Brave (web browser)|Brave]].com |access-date=27 July 2018 |archive-date=1 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200201011127/https://brave.com/features/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In September 2017, Bitwarden launched a [[bug bounty program]] at [[HackerOne]].<ref name="hackerone">{{cite web |title=Bitwarden |url=https://hackerone.com/bitwarden/?type=team |work=HackerOne.com |access-date=14 September 2022 |archive-date=14 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220914141513/https://hackerone.com/bitwarden/?type=team |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="BW-Compliance-2022-09-09" />

=== 2018 ===
In January 2018, the Bitwarden browser extension was adapted to and released for Apple's [[Safari (web browser)|Safari]] browser through the Safari Extensions Gallery.<ref name="bitwarden-safari-gallery">{{cite web |title=Safari Extensions Gallery |url= https://safari-extensions.apple.com/details/?id=com.bitwarden.safari-LTZ2PFU5D6 |work=Safari-extensions.[[Apple, Inc|Apple]].com |access-date=26 November 2018 |archive-date=27 November 2018 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20181127110616/https://safari-extensions.apple.com/details/?id=com.bitwarden.safari-LTZ2PFU5D6}}</ref> In February, Bitwarden debuted as a stand-alone desktop application for [[macOS]], [[Linux]], and [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]]. It was built as a [[Web application|web app]] variant of the browser extension, built with the [[Electron (software framework)|Electron framework]].<ref name="ghacks-desktopapp">{{cite web |last=Brinkmann |first=Martin |date=1 March 2018 |title=Bitwarden Desktop App released |work=[[Ghacks]] Technology News |url=https://www.ghacks.net/2018/03/01/bitwarden-desktop-app-released/ |access-date=29 July 2018 |archive-date=4 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304191421/https://www.ghacks.net/2018/03/01/bitwarden-desktop-app-released/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The Windows app was released alongside the Bitwarden extension for [[Microsoft Edge]] in the [[Microsoft Store (digital)|Microsoft Store]] a month later.<ref name="onmsft-microsoftstore">{{cite web |last=Stephenson |first=Brad |date=26 April 2018 |title=Password manager Bitwarden launches in the Microsoft Store |work=OnMsft.com |url=https://www.onmsft.com/news/password-manager-bitwarden-launches-in-the-microsoft-store |access-date=29 July 2018 |archive-date=5 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181105110758/https://www.onmsft.com/news/password-manager-bitwarden-launches-in-the-microsoft-store |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="windowscentral-edgeextension">{{cite web |last=Thorp-Lancaster |first=Dan |date=11 September 2017 |title=Bitwarden password manager extension comes to Microsoft Edge |work=[[Windows Central]] |url=https://www.windowscentral.com/bitwarden-password-manager-extension-comes-microsoft-edge |access-date=29 July 2018 |archive-date=31 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131080734/https://www.windowscentral.com/bitwarden-password-manager-extension-comes-microsoft-edge |url-status=live }}</ref> In May, Bitwarden released a [[Command-line interface|command-line]] application enabling users to write scripted applications using data from their Bitwarden vaults.<ref name="Downloads" /><ref>{{cite web |date=23 May 2013 |title=Bitwarden/cli v1.0.0 |work=[[GitHub]] |url= https://github.com/bitwarden/cli/releases/tag/v1.0.0 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220311020918/https://github.com/bitwarden/cli/releases/tag/v1.0.0 |archive-date=11 March 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Bitwarden Command-line Tool |url= https://blog.bitwarden.com/bitwarden-command-line-tool-now-available-e6184407b719 |work=The Bitwarden Blog |date=12 November 2018 |access-date=26 November 2018 |archive-date=24 May 2018 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20180524091726/https://blog.bitwarden.com/bitwarden-command-line-tool-now-available-e6184407b719}}</ref>  In June 2018, following a review, Bitwarden was made available as an optional password manager in the [[Cliqz]] browser<ref name="Cliqz extension review">{{cite web |last=Greif |first=Björn |date=6 June 2018 |title=Password manager Bitwarden now available in Cliqz Browser |work=[[Cliqz]] Blog |url=https://cliqz.com/en/magazine/password-manager-bitwarden-now-available-in-cliqz-browser |access-date=29 July 2018 |archive-date=5 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181105062338/https://cliqz.com/en/magazine/password-manager-bitwarden-now-available-in-cliqz-browser |url-status=live }}</ref> (discontinued in 2020).

=== 2022 ===
In September 2022, the company announced $100M [[Venture capital financing|series B financing]]; the lead investor was PSG (an affiliate of [[Providence Equity Partners]]), with the existing investor [[Battery Ventures]] participating.<ref name="Business Wire 6 September 2022">{{cite press release |title=Bitwarden Announces $100 Million Growth Investment Led by PSG to Further its Mission to Empower Businesses and Individuals to Stay Safe Online |date=6 September 2022 |publisher=Bitwarden |agency=[[Business Wire]] |url= https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20220906005153/en/Bitwarden-Announces-100-Million-Growth-Investment-Led-by-PSG-to-Further-its-Mission-to-Empower-Businesses-and-Individuals-to-Stay-Safe-Online |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220908124221/https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20220906005153/en/Bitwarden-Announces-100-Million-Growth-Investment-Led-by-PSG-to-Further-its-Mission-to-Empower-Businesses-and-Individuals-to-Stay-Safe-Online |archive-date=8 September 2022}}</ref><ref name="Bitwarden 6 September 2022">{{cite web |last=Crandell |first=Michael |date=6 September 2022 |title=Bitwarden announces $100 million financing |url= https://bitwarden.com/blog/accelerating-value-for-bitwarden-users-bitwarden-raises-usd100-million/ |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20220907203408/https://bitwarden.com/blog/accelerating-value-for-bitwarden-users-bitwarden-raises-usd100-million/ |archive-date=7 September 2022}}</ref> The investment would be used to accelerate [[product development]] and company growth to support its users and customers worldwide.<ref name="Business Wire 6 September 2022" /><ref name="Bitwarden 6 September 2022" />

=== 2023 ===
[[File:Bitwarden Passkey window screenshot.png|thumb|upright=1.2|Example of passwordless authentication with Bitwarden]]
In January, Bitwarden announced the acquisition of Swedish startup Passwordless.dev for an undisclosed amount.<ref name="TechCrunch 18 January 2023">{{cite web |date=18 January 2023 |title=Bitwarden acquires Passwordless.dev to help companies authenticate users without passwords |work=[[TechCrunch]] |url= https://techcrunch.com/2023/01/18/bitwarden-acquires-passwordless-dev-to-help-companies-authenticate-users-without-passwords/ |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230118220010/https://techcrunch.com/2023/01/18/bitwarden-acquires-passwordless-dev-to-help-companies-authenticate-users-without-passwords/ |archive-date=18 January 2023}}</ref> Passwordless.dev provided an open-source solution allowing developers to easily implement [[passwordless authentication]] based on the standards [[WebAuthn]] and [[FIDO2]].<ref name="TechCrunch 18 January 2023" /><ref>{{cite web |date=18 January 2023 |title=Bitwarden extends passwordless leadership with acquisition |work=Bitwarden.com |url= https://bitwarden.com/blog/bitwarden-extends-passwordless-leadership-with-acquisition/ |url-status=live |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20230119213527/https://bitwarden.com/blog/bitwarden-extends-passwordless-leadership-with-acquisition/ |archive-date=19 January 2023}}</ref>

Bitwarden also launched a [[Software release life cycle#Beta|beta]] software service allowing third-party developers the use of biometric sign-in technologies&nbsp;– including Apple's [[Touch ID]] and [[Face ID]], and Microsoft's [[Windows Hello]]&nbsp;– in their apps.<ref name="TechCrunch 18 January 2023" />

=== 2024 ===
On 1 May, Bitwarden launched its own [[multi-factor authentication]] app, Bitwarden Authenticator.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 May 2024 |title=Bitwarden launches its own free and open-source Authenticator app |access-date=19 May 2024 |work=Android Authority |url=https://www.androidauthority.com/bitwarden-authenticator-app-free-open-source-3439120/ |archive-date=19 May 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240519145959/https://www.androidauthority.com/bitwarden-authenticator-app-free-open-source-3439120/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In October of that year, Bitwarden introduced changes to the dependencies of its desktop application to include a restricted-use [[Software development kit|SDK]] that may prevent some members of the public from [[Compiler|compiling]] the application from [[source code]], provoking concerns that Bitwarden is moving away from open-source principles. Bitwarden [[Chief technical officer|CTO]] Kyle Spearrin stated in response that it is an issue they plan to resolve, and is "merely a bug".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Proven |first=Liam |date=24 October 2024 |title=Bitwarden's FOSS halo slips as new SDK requirement locks down freedoms |url=https://www.theregister.com/2024/10/24/bitwarden_foss_doubts/ |work=[[The Register]] |access-date=24 October 2024 |archive-date=11 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241211212055/https://www.theregister.com/2024/10/24/bitwarden_foss_doubts/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== 2026 ===
Bitwarden raised the price of its "Premium" subscription in February 2026 from $10 to $20 per year, which was criticized by ''[[Fast Company]]'' and [[Reddit]] users for being announced in a section of a blog post covering feature updates instead of being communicated more transparently.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Newman |first1=Jared |title=Bitwarden announced a price hike in the worst way possible |url=https://www.fastcompany.com/91483458/bitwarden-price-increase |website=[[Fast Company]] |access-date=8 August 2026 |date=1 February 2026}}</ref> Bitwarden Inc. CEOs Michael Crandell and Stephen Morrison stepped down from their roles in February and April 2026, and were replaced Michael Sullivan and Michael Shenkman, respectively. In May 2026, ''Fast Company'' reported that Bitwarden had removed the phrase "Always free" from its marketing page for its free plan and replaced the terms "inclusion" and "transparency" from its list of principles on its hiring page with "innovation" and "trust". Sullivan's [[LinkedIn]] profile touted his experience with [[mergers and acquisitions]], particularly involving [[private equity firm]]s, and prior to his appointment, he served as CEO at two companies that were involved in private equity transactions valued at $1 billion each. After being contacted by ''Fast Company'', Bitwarden restored "Always free" to the description of its free plan.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Newman |first1=Jared |title=Bitwarden scrubs 'Always free' and 'Inclusion' values from its website as longtime execs step down |url=https://www.fastcompany.com/91542655/bitwarden-scrubs-always-free-and-inclusion-values-from-its-website-as-longtime-execs-step-down |website=[[Fast Company]] |access-date=8 August 2026 |date=15 May 2026}}</ref>

== Security ==
=== 2024 evaluation of password checkup tools ===
A 2024 study by Hutchinson et al. examined the “password checkup” features of 14 password managers, including Bitwarden, using weak, breached, and randomly generated passwords. The authors found that the evaluated products reported weak and compromised passwords inconsistently and sometimes incompletely. No manager successfully flagged all known breached passwords. The study concludes that such inconsistencies may give users a false sense of security.<ref name="Hutchinson2024"/>

=== 2025 DOM-based extension clickjacking ===
Security researcher Marek Tóth presented a vulnerability in browser extensions of several password managers (including Bitwarden) at [[DEF CON]] 33 on August 9, 2025. In their default configurations, these extensions were shown to be exposed to a DOM-based extension clickjacking technique, allowing attackers to exfiltrate user data with just a single click.<ref>{{Cite web |author1=Benedict Collins |date=2025-08-22 |title=Multiple top password managers vulnerable to password stealing clickjacking attacks - here's what we know |url=https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/multiple-top-password-managers-vulnerable-to-password-stealing-clickjacking-attacks-heres-what-we-know |access-date=2025-11-09 |website=TechRadar |language=en |archive-date=13 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251113052831/https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/multiple-top-password-managers-vulnerable-to-password-stealing-clickjacking-attacks-heres-what-we-know |url-status=live }}</ref> The affected password manager vendors were notified in April 2025. According to Tóth, Bitwarden version 2025.8.2 (August 31, 2025) addressed the issue.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tóth |first=Marek |date=2025-08-09 |title=DOM-based Extension Clickjacking: Your Password Manager Data at Risk |url=https://marektoth.com/blog/dom-based-extension-clickjacking/ |access-date=2025-11-09 |website=marektoth.com |language=en |archive-date=15 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251115052239/https://marektoth.com/blog/dom-based-extension-clickjacking/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2026 Vault Compromise Under Malicious Server ===
Researchers from [[ETH Zurich]] and [[Università della Svizzera italiana]] found 12 attacks work against Bitwarden, 7 attacks work against [[LastPass]], and 6 attacks work against [[Dashlane]], all Cloud-based<ref name="wired/password">{{cite news |last1=Gilbertson |first1=Scott |title=The Password Managers You Should Use Instead of Your Browser |url=https://www.wired.com/story/best-password-managers/ |access-date=4 September 2026 |work=[[Wired.com]] |date=2 August 2026}}</ref> Password Managers.<ref name="ethz/managers-less-secure">{{cite web |title=Password managers less secure than promised |url=https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2026/02/password-managers-less-secure-than-promised.html |website=[[ETH Zurich]] |access-date=4 September 2026 |language=en |date=16 February 2026}}</ref><ref>[https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/058.pdf <!-- https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/058  https://www.usenix.org/system/files/usenixsecurity26-scarlata.pdf -->Zero Knowledge (About) Encryption: A Comparative Security Analysis of Four Cloud-based Password Managers]</ref><ref name="sW/malicious-server">{{cite news |last1=Kovacs |first1=Eduard |title=Password Managers Vulnerable to Vault Compromise Under Malicious Server |url=https://www.securityweek.com/password-managers-vulnerable-to-vault-compromise-under-malicious-server/ |access-date=4 September 2026 |work=SecurityWeek |date=17 February 2026}}</ref>
